title: Noetherian spreading data for a generically split finite torsor
statement: Let $S$ be a qcqs integral scheme whose local rings are integrally closed, and let $c:C\to S$ be a qcqs smooth morphism with geometrically connected fibres and section $\sigma:S\to C$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $K$ for the function field and $i:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ for the generic-point map. Let $q:C_\eta\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $j:C_\eta\to C$ give a pullback square with $i,c$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $s_\eta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to C_\eta$ satisfy $s_\eta q=1$ and $s_\eta j=i\sigma$. Let $G$ be a finite group whose order is invertible on $S$, and $Z\to C_\eta$ a finite etale $G$-torsor with a $K$-rational point over $s_\eta$ [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. There exist a Noetherian qcqs normal integral scheme $S_0$, a qcqs smooth family $c_0:C_0\to S_0$ with geometrically connected fibres, a section $\sigma_0$, its generic fibre $q_0:C_{\eta,0}\to\operatorname{Spec}K_0$, $j_0:C_{\eta,0}\to C_0$ as a pullback over the generic-point map, a generic section $s_{\eta,0}$ compatible with $\sigma_0$, and a finite etale $G$-torsor $Z_0\to C_{\eta,0}$ with a $K_0$-rational point over $s_{\eta,0}$. The order of $G$ is invertible on $S_0$. There are comparison maps $a:C\to C_0$, $k:C_\eta\to C_{\eta,0}$ and $\chi:Z\to Z_0$ such that $kj_0=ja$ and the square with $\chi,k$ and the two torsor projections is cartesian. This assertion constructs only approximation data, not a cover of $C_0$ or $C$.

proof.text: Apply exists_normal_family_generic_limit with n=Nat.card G. Retain the two generic-fibre limit cones, their compatible sections, and all normal Noetherian family data at every stage. This construction does not involve Z.

Apply exists_pointed_stage_of_affine_limits to these two systems and Z. It selects a stage i, a finite Galois torsor Z₀ on its generic fibre, a cartesian comparison χ, and a point z₀ from K_i above s_i.

Choose S₀=S_i and C₀=C_i and use the family data at i. Set the generic section to e_i.inv ≫ s_i, and transport the descended point to e_i.inv ≫ z₀. Associativity and z₀ ≫ Z₀.π=s_i give its required equality. The two generic-section equalities follow by associativity from the family data. Take a=a_i and k=κ_i. The comparison k ≫ j₀=j ≫ a and the cartesian cover square are exactly the two previously retained hypotheses.
